correctness.rationale: For a finite simple graph with one unit symmetric good per edge and endpoint-only orientation, every nontrivial tree forces a zero-indegree vertex paid >=1 and, if any exists, all I isolated agents must also be paid >=1. Root-directed tree orientations and cycle-directed cyclic components attain S=1_{T>0}(T+I). At p=(log n+loglog n+c)/(2n), isolated edges have Poisson mean e^-c/4 by factorial moments; larger trees disappear by uniform bounds; isolates concentrate at a_n=e^-c/2 sqrt(n/log n). The normalized subsidy tends to Bernoulli(1−exp(-e^-c/4)) and expectation converges in L1.

evidence: Li et al. treat worst-case subsidies and algorithms for richer graphical valuations; the prior Poisson envy theorem gives only T(G_n) and zero-envy probability, not the scaling of subsidy by sqrt(n/log n).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior generalized fair-division setting does not automatically supply this exact random cost distribution; older observation of one isolated good paying isolates is credited.

evidence: Prior T(G_n)->Poisson(e^-c/4) is one ingredient. The extra identity S(G)=0 or T+I and concentration I_n/e^-c/2 sqrt(n/log n)->1 force the Bernoulli amplification.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The previously published zero-envy probability is the same zero-subsidy probability, explicitly credited. The scaled cost distribution and asymptotic expected volume depend on new subsidy analysis and isolate concentration.

evidence: Earlier Resultary theorem minimizes number of envious agents T(G) with no payments; subsidy requires compensated utilities across every pair and the extra I(G) burden when T>0.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Minimizing envious-agent count is not equivalent to minimizing external monetary subsidy despite common structural obstructions.

originality.rationale: Published exact minimum number of envious agents and Poisson tree-component law are prior work; the new observable is total external monetary subsidy for global envy freedom, not the count of envious agents. Its finite exact identity S(G)=1_{T>0}(T+I), with isolates amplified, yields the distinct two-point non-self-averaging limit.
residual_risks: Full mathematical text of Li et al. 2025 and IJCAI 2026 was not read; an exact finite subsidy identity could have appeared earlier.
The zero-subsidy probability equals the already published zero-envy event and has no separate originality credit.

value.rationale: The finite-graph payment identity distinguishes uncompensated envy count from monetary cost. A rare isolated-edge Poisson obstruction causing payments to an unbounded number of otherwise empty agents is a motivated and sharp stochastic amplification phenomenon.

limitations: Requires simple graph, binary symmetric endpoint goods, global comparisons, nonnegative external payments.
The critical window includes many isolated vertices but typically finitely many nontrivial tree components; no claims for arbitrary valuations or dense random graphs.
